오는 길에 내 목소리를 들었소.\n숲 안쪽에서 나를 부르더군.\n이런 일:
I heard my own voice on the way here.
It was calling me from deep in the forest.
Is that a common thing?
어서 돌아오라고 했소.\n난 그곳에 간 적도 없는데.\n누군가를 잘못 안:
It told me to hurry back.
I've never been there in my life.
They must have mistaken me for someone else.
그럴 생각이오.\n문이 두꺼워서 마음에 드는군.\n창가에선 떨어져 자겠소:
That's my plan.
I like how thick the door is.
I'll sleep away from the window.
I won't ask what you put in the food.
Something warm is enough for tonight.
창문 밖에 약초가 자라고 있어요.\n분명 겨울엔 피지 않는 종류인데…\n:
There are herbs growing outside the window.
They're the kind that shouldn't bloom in winter…
Do you grow them here at the Lodge?
햇빛을 따라 고개를 돌려요.\n그런데 저건 계속 숲을 보고 있죠.\n뿌리:
They turn their heads toward the sunlight.
But that one keeps looking at the forest.
I wouldn't go near its roots.
Let's look at it together in the morning.
Good. I didn't want to go out alone.
I'll pack my gathering tools.
I think coming here was a good idea.
There's someone to ask when I'm curious.
마차 옆에 발자국이 있었소.\n숲으로 들어간 흔적뿐이었지.\n돌아 나온:
There were footprints beside the wagon.
Only ones leading into the forest.
None coming back out.
그렇다면 소리를 냈겠지.\n그런데 마차의 말들만 울더군.\n사람들은 아무:
Then they would have called out.
But only the wagon's horses were crying.
No one heard a sound.
You should avoid that road for a while.
I told the escort captain the same.
The next wagon will go another way.
A story like that calls for soup.
Another bowl of the same as before.
해 질 무렵 종이 울렸소.\n길을 아는 나도 방향을 잃었지.\n근처에 성:
A bell rang at dusk.
I know these roads, yet I lost my way.
Has a church been built nearby?
어느 쪽에서 들었지?: Which direction did you hear it from?
처음엔 북쪽이었소.\n다시 들릴 때는 내 등 뒤였고.\n돌아보니 길만 있:
North at first.
The second time it was behind me.
When I turned around, there was only the road.
I'm glad you didn't follow the sound.
오래 호위 일을 했소.\n낯선 초대엔 대가가 따르지.\n이번엔 발을 돌렸:
I've guarded for many years.
A strange invitation always has a price.
This time I turned my feet away.
오늘은 창문에서 먼 방을 부탁하오.\n문 잠그는 소리가 들리는 쪽이면 좋:
Please give me a room far from the window tonight.
One where I can hear the door being locked would be nice.
배달 가방에 모르는 편지가 있어요.\n받는 사람 이름이 없는데…\n봉투엔:
There's a strange letter in my delivery bag.
It has no recipient's name…
The envelope has this Lodge drawn on it.
누가 맡겼는지 기억나?: Do you remember who handed it to you?
그게 이상해요. 기억이 안 나요.\n하지만 누가 웃었던 건 기억나요.\n:
That's the odd part. I can't remember.
But I remember someone laughing.
I can't picture the face.
Don't open it. Keep it safe.
알겠어요. 제일 안쪽에 넣어 둘게요.\n이런 편지는 서두르면 안 될 것:
All right. I'll tuck it in the very back.
A letter like this shouldn't be rushed, I think.
오늘은 배달 이야기는 여기까지!\n따뜻한 차를 마시면 좀 낫겠죠?:
That's enough delivery talk for today!
A warm cup of tea will help, won't it?
폐허에서 문양을 베껴 왔소.\n그런데 오던 길에 다시 보니\n내 기록과:
I copied the markings from the ruins.
But when I looked again on the way here,
the direction differed from my notes.
물론이오. 나도 그렇게 생각했지.\n그래서 세 번 베꼈소.\n세 장이 서:
Of course. I thought so too.
So I copied them three times.
All three came out different from one another.
그 기록을 더 살펴봐도 될까?: May I take a closer look at those notes?
기꺼이요. 내일 다시 펴 보겠소.\n오늘은 잉크가 마르길 기다립시다.\n:
Gladly. I'll unfold them again tomorrow.
Tonight let's wait for the ink to dry.
I want to study even the smudges.
Keep the fire lit tomorrow too.
I've grown more curious about this hearth than the forest.
I had six glass bottles when I set out.
I counted them here and there are seven.
I never bought one from anyone.
어떤 병이 새로 생겼어?: Which bottle is the new one?
그걸 모르겠어요.\n모양도 마개도 전부 같거든요.\n다만 하나만 손에 차:
That's what I can't tell.
The shape and stopper are all the same.
Only one feels cold in my hand.
저도 그렇게 생각했어요.\n물건이 늘어도 기쁘지 않은 건\n장사하면서 처:
I thought so too.
Gaining goods that bring no joy —
that's a first in all my years of trading.
I'll pay for my stay with my own money.
Not with the coin I found at the bottom of my bag.
벽을 다 두드려 봤소.\n한 군데만 소리가 달라.\n부엌 뒤, 바닥 가까:
I tapped every wall.
Only one spot sounds different.
Behind the kitchen, near the floor.
That's where the way down to the cellar is.
그렇군. 그럼 됐소.\n속이 빈 게 아니라 길이 있는 거지.\n길은 막을:
I see. Then that's fine.
It isn't hollow, it's a passage.
A passage can be blocked.
그 벽 앞에서 자 줄 수 있어?: Could you sleep in front of that wall?
I'll set up my shield and sleep there.
A dwarf only sleeps well
with his back to a wall.
The house is sturdy.
As long as its keeper isn't weaker than the walls.
숲에서 동전을 던졌소.\n앞면이면 돌아가고\n뒷면이면 오기로. 열 번 다:
I flipped a coin in the forest.
Heads I'd turn back,
tails I'd come on. Ten tails in a row.
자. …어? 양쪽 다 뒷면이군.\n내 동전이 아니야.\n누가 바꿔치기했어:
Here. …Huh? Tails on both sides.
This isn't my coin.
Someone swapped it, out in the forest.
Ha! Saying that
ruins the bet.
…Thank you. The drinks are on me.
Let's make the next bet an easy one.
Who snores first tonight.
오늘 벤 나무 말이오.\n나이테가 안쪽으로 갈수록\n젊었소. 거꾸로 자란:
The tree I felled today.
Its rings got younger
toward the center. It grew backward.
I was waiting for you to say that.
I set it aside in the corner of the barn.
Swept up the sawdust too.
그런 나무가 더 있어?: Are there more trees like it?
The deeper into the forest, the more there are.
The trees are growing
leaning toward something.
Tomorrow I'll fell only straight-grained trees.
Leave the beams to me, keeper.
창턱 이끼를 긁었는데\n밤새 다시 자랐어.\n이끼는 그렇게 안 자라, 얘:
I scraped the moss off the windowsill
and it grew back overnight.
Moss doesn't grow like that, dear.
약으로 쓸 수 있을까?: Could it be used as medicine?
쓸 수는 있지.\n근데 뭘 먹고 자란 건지 몰라.\n내가 먼저 조금 먹어:
It could.
But I don't know what it feeds on.
I'll try a little first myself.
Yes, that's better.
Let it grow and we'll watch.
Until we know what it's up to.
The tea's gone cold. Again.
…Never mind, I'll warm it up.
I laid a hand on the foundation stone
and it was warm. In winter.
Stones don't lie.
There's an old stone in the cellar.
역시. 그 돌이 숨을 쉬는군.\n내가 본 유적의 돌도 그랬소.\n…그 유:
As I thought. That stone breathes.
The stones of the ruin I saw did the same.
…That ruin is gone now.
We'd better stop talking about that.
…Understood.
Stone knows how to wait.
So will I.
I won't write it down.
The stone will remember.
경첩을 고쳤소.\n그런데 밤에 또 소리가 나.\n경첩이 아니오. 문이 떨:
I fixed the hinge.
But it creaks again at night.
Not the hinge. The door is trembling.
At night, things outside push on the door.
…I see.
I'll add an iron plate.
No charge.
Thanks, but don't do anything dangerous.
…Hammering isn't dangerous.
A door left unfixed is.
